newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-PAGELSDORF TO BE NEW COACH AT HAMBURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PAGELSDORF TO BE NEW COACH AT HAMBURG.

text.p: Struggling giants Hamburg said on Tuesday Frank Pagelsdorf would be their new coach, moving from fellow Bundesliga side Hansa Rostock to replace Felix Magath.
"It's all done and dusted," a Hamburg spokesman told Reuters. "He'll be the new coach."

The club, only a shadow of the side which had success in the 1970s and 1980s including a 1983 European Cup triumph, had been linked with big names such as former Hamburg player Kevin Keegan after Magath was dismissed last week.

But Hamburg made clear their admiration for Pagelsdorf, a former Borussia Dortmund player who led Rostock to the second division title in his first season and has kept them in the top flight over the past two seasons despite limited resources.

Club president Uwe Seeler, the former German World Cup-winning striker, is keen to put Hamburg back on the international map but Pagelsdorf said it would take time to transform a side lying 15th in the Bundesliga.
"The first year is a reconstruction year," he said. "You can't expect to be challenging for UEFA Cup places straight away."
Rostock cleared the way for the burly 39-year-old on Monday night, agreeing to release him from his current contract which ran until next year.
"With this decision, Hansa Rostock is granting Mr Pagelsdorf's wish to take on a new sporting challenge with Hamburg," the club said in a statement.
Hamburg said Pagelsdorf was likely to receive a three-year contract which would be signed during the close season after the coach had taken a holiday.
"We're pleased he's chosen Hamburg," Seeler said. "He's the right man for the job."
